items.problem: Test-AppLaunch could not discover a valid default dotnet build layout.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turn 65 reported status=unavailable after turn 61's successful build; it worked only after turn 68 rebuilt with Platform=x64.
items.skill_search: Test-AppLaunch.ps1 lines 118-134 searched only bin\x64\Debug and bin\ARM64\Debug.
items.wrong_text_if_any: No build output found under bin\x64\Debug - build the project first.
items.root_cause: The script inferred one output path convention instead of locating a directory containing both the executable and package manifest.
items.proposed_fix: Search recursively under the project's bin directory for the newest launchable layout and make Validate-UwpMigration delegate target-mode discovery to the same helper.
items.generalizes: SDK-style WinUI builds vary by explicit Platform, configuration, TFM, and RID; default builds commonly omit the platform directory.

items.problem: The skill gave an absolute and incorrect diagnosis for XAML Internal Error WMC9999.
items.evidence: WMC9999 appeared beside CS0234/CS0246/CS0103 and explicit WMC0909/WMC1111 errors in turns 40-57, then disappeared after those errors and a temporary XAML file were fixed.
items.wrong_text_if_any: Treat WMC9999 on a XAML build as a dangling resource key, not a code bug.
items.root_cause: WMC9999 is a generic markup-compiler cascade and does not uniquely identify a missing resource.
items.proposed_fix: Tell agents to fix all specific CS####/WMC#### errors first and audit resources only if WMC9999 remains by itself.
items.generalizes: Many WinUI XAML compiler failures emit WMC9999 as a secondary error, so premature resource-key edits waste time across unrelated migrations.
